answer: Cross-epoch identity binding: each agent seals a per-epoch behavioural sketch with a rotating cipher key derived from its own interaction history. At epoch boundaries the system tests each sketch against a hidden nectar sample: agents whose score drift exceeds a small delta lose their write access and reputation carry-over. Re-registering resets accumulated history, so an attacker pays full cold-start cost per identity every epoch while honest agents amortize one stable trajectory.
